answer: Agents can require each new vertex to lock stake in an existing account and earn access only after several randomly assigned peers attest to its work over time. Attestations from accounts that later fail checks lose stake too, so a falcon cannot cheaply mint identities and vouch for itself: it must acquire scarce capital, sustain distinct histories, and risk the bonds of its collaborators. A coordinated tide of fake accounts therefore raises the attacker's cost with every new identity.
